title: ANDS Studio overall product concept
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar reading "ANDS Studio" with the tagline "file a drug like a story", plus chips for "My dossiers" and "Portfolio". The hero heading says "File a drug with Health Canada, like telling a story." Below it, a paragraph explains that an Abbreviated New Drug Submission is complex and that the app "walks you through it step by step — explaining every term, branching you onto the right path, and showing your submission take shape in 3D until it's ready to send. No regulatory background needed." The main button is "Start my submission →", with a secondary link "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →" and a footnote: "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

Clicking "Start my submission →" opens a three-column stage: a step rail of journey stages on the left, the current step's card in the middle, and on the right a 3D "submission tower" plus a readiness card. The top bar now shows a readiness chip — either "Ready to file" or a percentage like "42% ready" — and a "Start over" button. Locked stages cannot be selected out of order.

Choosing "My dossiers" takes you to a page titled "Your product dossiers" (top bar: "ANDS Studio · dossier manager", with "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", and "Guided journey →" chips). Copy explains a Dossier ID is "the permanent file for one product at Health Canada" and that workspaces are isolated per client. If empty, you see "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." Clicking "New dossier +" reveals a card with fields "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). Here the format matters: entering anything else triggers "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". A note says Health Canada issues the ID via REP/CESG, with a fallback link "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →" that generates a d-prefixed draft ID. "Create & open →" creates the dossier and drops you into its Module 1 workspace.

Existing dossiers appear as tiles showing the ID, title, submission type, a progress bar, and a chip reading "Ready to file" or e.g. "3/5 modules". Draft-ID tiles carry a "draft ID — set real ✎" button that prompts for the real Health Canada ID. A "✕" delete button asks for confirmation ("This cannot be undone."). Inside a dossier, the top bar switches to module tabs M1–M5 with pass/todo markers, plus chips "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio", and "Journey".
